renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: abundance_ribbon
  title: Clone rank abundance
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the estimated share of the repertoire held by the clone at each rank, with a shaded band for its uncertainty. It answers how dominant the largest clones are and how well the estimate is backed.
    How to read: a steep curve that starts high and falls fast is an expanded repertoire dominated by a few clones. A flat, low curve is polyclonal. A wide band means the estimate rests on few sequences, so compare samples only where their bands do not overlap.
    Lines and annotations: the shaded band is the confidence interval alakazam derives by bootstrapping the clone abundances (a 95% interval from 100 bootstrap realizations in its vignette example). It is a property of the estimate and not a cut-off.
    Source: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Clone rank
    y_title: Relative abundance
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample_id
    x: rank
    y: p
    lower: lower
    upper: upper

- component: card
  title: Largest clone share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest relative abundance of any clone in view, and the box shows its quartiles over the rows in view. It answers how much of a repertoire the top clone can hold.
    How to read: a high maximum points to one dominant clone, which is expected in an immune response and unusual in a resting repertoire. Filter to one sample to read its own top clone.
  column: p
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: largest clone share, per sample

- component: card
  title: Abundance uncertainty
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median bootstrap standard deviation of a clone's relative abundance, with the lowest and highest values next to it. It answers how stable the abundance estimates are.
    How to read: a standard deviation close to the abundance itself means the clone is poorly estimated, usually from a shallow sample. A low value across clones means the curves above can be trusted.
  column: p_sd
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: bootstrap spread, lowest to highest

- component: table
  title: Clone abundance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a clone of a sample at one rank, with its relative abundance, its bootstrap standard deviation and the lower and upper bounds of its band. It answers which clones lead each sample and by how much.
    How to read: sort by rank to see the head of each sample, or by abundance to compare samples of one subject.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: diversity_profile
  title: Diversity profile by order
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: its Hill diversity at every order q, coloured by subject. It answers how diverse each repertoire is and how that changes as common clones weigh more.
    How to read: the horizontal axis is the diversity order q, not a sequencing depth. At q = 0 every clone counts equally (richness), at q = 1 it is the exponential of Shannon entropy and at q = 2 the inverse Simpson index. A curve that falls steeply is dominated by a few clones, a flat one is even, and curves that run apart at high q differ in their dominant clones.
    Sources: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/ and https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/calcDiversity/
  kind: rarefaction
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    depth: q
    metric: d
    group: subject_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: diversity_ci_bars
  title: Diversity with confidence interval
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: its Hill diversity with a whisker for the bootstrap confidence interval. It answers which samples differ in diversity beyond the uncertainty of the estimate.
    How to read: filter to one diversity order first (0 richness, 1 Shannon, 2 inverse Simpson), otherwise every order is drawn at once. Samples whose whiskers do not overlap differ, but overlapping whiskers do not rule a difference out: alakazam tests one with a bootstrap delta distribution, not by overlap.
    Lines and annotations: the whiskers are the confidence interval alakazam derives by bootstrapping, as shown in its diversity vignette.
    Sources: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/ and https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/calcDiversity/
  kind: metric_ci_bars
  config:
    metric_name: Hill diversity
  roles:
    label: sample_id
    value: d
    lower: d_lower
    upper: d_upper

- component: table
  title: Diversity table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample at one diversity order, with its Hill diversity, bootstrap standard deviation, confidence bounds and evenness. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: filter to one order to compare samples, and read the evenness column to separate a rich but dominated repertoire from a flat one.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: overlap_heatmap
  title: Shared clones between samples
  description: |-
    Each cell is a pair of samples: the number of clones they share. It answers which samples carry the same clones, and so which belong to one lineage of cells.
    How to read: dark blocks along a subject are samples that share many clones, as expected for replicates or related tissues of one individual. A sample with pale cells against its own subject shares little and may be a different compartment or a poor library. Cells between subjects stay empty because clones are defined within a subject.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is set to zero, since a sample shares all of its clones with itself and would flatten the colour scale. The annotation strip names the subject of each row.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample_id
    row_annotation_cols:
    - subject_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: overlap_mds
  title: Samples by clonal overlap
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample, placed so that samples sharing many clones sit close together, and coloured by subject. It answers how the samples group by their shared clones.
    How to read: tight groups are samples with similar clonal content, usually the same subject. A sample far from its subject-mates has few shared clones. The axes are ordination coordinates, so read the distances between points and not the axis values.
    Note: the coordinates are computed from the matrix at render time and follow the active sample filter.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PCo
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    cluster: subject_id
    color: subject_id

- component: table
  title: Clonal overlap table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with the number of clones it shares with every other sample. It answers the exact counts behind the heatmap.
    How to read: read across a row to see which samples it shares clones with, and filter by subject to compare like with like.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: shared_clones_upset
  title: Clones shared between samples
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of samples and its height is the number of clones found in exactly those samples. It answers which samples share clones and how many clones are private to one.
    How to read: a tall bar over a single dot is a private clone set. Bars over several dots are clones shared by those samples, which points to the same lineage seen in several tissues or time points. The side bars give the total clones per sample.
    Lines and annotations: bars are coloured by the number of samples in the combination, so private and widely shared clones separate at a glance.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: card
  title: Samples sharing a clone
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest number of samples any single clone appears in, and the box shows the quartiles over all clones. It answers how widely clones are shared.
    How to read: a maximum of one means no clone is shared. A box that sits at one with a long tail means sharing is the exception.
  column: n_samples
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: samples per clone, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Shared clones table
  description: |-
    Each row is a clone of one subject, with the number of samples it appears in, its total sequences and a 0/1 flag per sample. It answers which clones are shared and where.
    How to read: sort by the number of samples or by total sequences to find the widest and the largest clones.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: clone_composition
  title: Clone size classes by sample
  description: |-
    Each arc is a group of sequences: the inner ring is the subject, the middle ring the sample and the outer ring the clone size class, sized by sequence count and coloured by size class. It answers how much of each repertoire sits in large clones.
    How to read: a sample whose outer ring is mostly the largest class is dominated by expanded clones. A ring spread over small classes is polyclonal. Click an arc to zoom in on it.
    Lines and annotations: the size classes are clonal homeostasis bins on clone frequency, from rare to hyperexpanded, using the default class boundaries of the immunarch repClonality function (1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-3 and 0.01 of the repertoire). They are descriptive groupings and not a clinical cut-off.
    Source: https://immunarch.com/reference/repClonality.html
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: size_class
  roles:
    ranks:
    - subject_id
    - sample_id
    - size_class
    abundance: seq_count

- component: card
  title: Largest clone size
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sequence count of the largest clone in view, with the mean and upper quartile of clone sizes. It answers how large the biggest expansion is against a typical clone.
    How to read: most clones hold a single sequence, so the mean stays near the bottom. A maximum far above the upper quartile marks a clearly expanded clone.
  column: seq_count
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - average
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: largest clone, with the mean and upper quartile

- component: card
  title: Clones by size class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct clones, and the bars rank the size classes by how many clones they hold. It answers whether the repertoire is made of many small clones or a few large ones.
    How to read: a ranking led by the small classes is the usual polyclonal shape. Large classes near the top point to expansion. Filter to one sample to compare.
  column: clone_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: size_class
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: clones, by size class

- component: table
  title: Clone size table
  description: |-
    Each row is a clone of a sample, with its sequence count, frequency, rank and size class. It answers which clones lead each sample.
    How to read: sort by rank or by frequency, and filter by size class to list the expanded clones.

outputs.name: Hill diversity at the named orders

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: diversity_order_ci_bars
  title: Hill diversity per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: its Hill diversity at the chosen order, with a whisker for the bootstrap confidence interval. It answers which samples differ in diversity beyond the uncertainty of the estimate.
    How to read: pick one order with the filter. Order 0 counts every clone, order 1 is the exponential of Shannon entropy and order 2 the inverse Simpson index, so higher orders weigh common clones more. Samples with non-overlapping whiskers differ, while overlapping ones do not rule a difference out, since alakazam tests it with a bootstrap delta distribution.
    Lines and annotations: the whiskers are the confidence interval alakazam derives by bootstrapping, as shown in its diversity vignette.
    Sources: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/ and https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/calcDiversity/
  kind: metric_ci_bars
  config:
    metric_name: Hill diversity
  roles:
    label: sample_id
    value: d
    lower: d_lower
    upper: d_upper

- component: interactive
  id: diversity_order_picker
  title: Diversity order
  description: |-
    Chooses which Hill order the tiles read: richness (q = 0), Shannon (q = 1) or inverse Simpson (q = 2).
    How to read: start at richness, then move to q = 2 to see whether the ranking of samples changes once dominant clones weigh more.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: order

- component: table
  title: Hill diversity table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample at one named order, with its Hill diversity and the lower and upper bounds of its confidence interval. It answers the exact values behind the bars.
    How to read: filter by order and sort by diversity to rank the samples.

- component: card
  title: Clones
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of clones across the samples in view, and the box shows the quartiles of clones per sample. It answers how many distinct lineages were recovered.
    How to read: compare samples in the box, since a low outlier is usually a shallow library. Clones are defined within a subject.
  column: number_of_clones
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: clones per sample, with their spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Sequences per clone
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the mean clone size, the number of sequences per clone, and the box shows its spread. It answers how expanded the clones are on average.
    How to read: a value near one means almost every clone is a single sequence, as in a polyclonal repertoire. Higher values mean larger clones, or deeper sequencing of the same clones.
  column: sequences_per_clone
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean clone size, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Shannon diversity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the Hill number at q = 1, the exponential of Shannon entropy, and the box shows its spread. It answers how diverse the repertoires are while giving common clones their weight.
    How to read: compare the median with the clone counts above. A diversity far below the clone count means a few clones dominate.
    Sources: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/ and https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/calcDiversity/
  column: shannon
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: Shannon diversity, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Evenness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the evenness of the Hill profile at q = 1, and the box shows its spread. It answers whether clones are of similar size or dominated by a few.
    How to read: values near one mean clones of similar size. Lower values mean a few large clones carry the repertoire, so check the rank abundance curve. This table publishes no accepted cut-off, so compare samples with each other.
  column: evenness
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: evenness, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Clones against sequencing depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: the sequences that entered clonal assignment on the horizontal axis and the clones they collapsed into on the vertical axis, sized by sequences per clone and coloured by subject. It answers whether the number of clones simply follows depth.
    How to read: points rise together because deeper samples reveal more clones. A sample sitting well below its neighbours at the same depth is more clonal, and a large marker means its clones are bigger. Both axes are logarithmic.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sequences
    y: number_of_clones
    color: subject_id
    size: sequences_per_clone
    log_x: 'True'
    log_y: 'True'
    labels:
      sequences: Sequences
      number_of_clones: Clones
      subject_id: Subject
      sequences_per_clone: Sequences per clone

- component: advanced_viz
  id: richness_evenness
  title: Richness against evenness
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its richness on the horizontal axis and its evenness on the vertical axis, sized by sequencing depth and coloured by subject. It answers whether a rich repertoire is also flat or carried by a few clones.
    How to read: points to the upper right are both rich and even. Points to the lower right are rich but dominated by a few clones. Read richness against marker size, because a deeper sample reveals more clones.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median evenness of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Immcantation.
    Source: https://alakazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/Diversity-Vignette/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Richness (Hill order 0)
    y_title: Evenness
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: richness
    y: evenness
    label: sample_id
    color: subject_id
    size: sequences

- component: table
  title: Repertoire summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its sequence and clone counts, clone-size spread and Hill numbers with their confidence bounds. It answers which samples to inspect and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by clones or diversity to find outliers, then select a row to focus the other tiles on that sample.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample_id

- component: card
  title: Read attrition
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total raw reads in view, and the strip shows how many are left after each pRESTO and Change-O stage. It answers where the reads are lost on the way to the final repertoire.
    How to read: the consensus, representative and collapse stages merge reads into UMI groups or unique sequences, so a large drop there is expected. A drop at quality filtering, primer masking or pairing points to a library problem.
  column: sequences
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - quality_filtered
  - primers_masked
  - paired
  - consensus
  - assembled
  - representative
  - productive
  - collapsed
  caption: reads left after each stage

- component: card
  title: Raw reads per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median raw read count per sample, and the box shows its spread. It answers how evenly the samples were sequenced.
    How to read: a sample far below the box has too little depth to compare. A very wide box means uneven sequencing, so use the diversity at a matched depth.
  column: sequences
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: raw reads per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Final unique sequences
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of unique sequences left after the last stage, and the box shows their spread across samples. It answers how much repertoire remains for the analysis.
    How to read: samples with very few final sequences give wide confidence intervals in the diversity tiles. Compare with the raw reads to see how much each sample lost.
  column: collapsed
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: final sequences per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Read retention
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median fraction of raw reads still represented at the last stage, and the box shows its spread. It answers how efficiently the pipeline turns reads into repertoire.
    How to read: retention is low by design here, since reads collapse onto UMI groups and unique sequences. Compare samples with each other, and investigate a sample whose retention is far below the rest.
  column: retention
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: retention, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Sequence counts table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its sequence count after every pRESTO and Change-O stage and its overall retention. It answers where each sample lost its reads.
    How to read: read across a row to find the stage with the biggest drop, and sort by retention to find the outliers.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: attrition_sankey
  title: Where reads are lost
  description: |-
    Each band is a group of reads moving from one pRESTO stage to the next, and its width is the number of reads. It answers at which stage reads are lost and how many reach the final representative sequences.
    How to read: a wide band leaving to Lost marks a stage that discards many reads. Stages that merge reads onto UMI groups also shed width without being a failure. A loss at quality filtering or pairing points to the library, so open the counts table.
    Note: bands are coloured by the stage they lead to, because every flow starts at the same input node.
  kind: sankey
  config:
    color_mode: target
    value_col: reads
    value_label: Reads
    value_format: count
  roles:
    steps:
    - input
    - quality
    - paired
    - consensus
    - assembled
    - representative

- component: table
  title: Read fate table
  description: |-
    Each row is a path through the stages for one sample, with the number of reads that took it. It answers how many reads follow each route.
    How to read: filter to one sample and sort by reads to see its main routes.

- component: card
  title: Clonal distance threshold
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean nearest-neighbour distance threshold over the subjects in view, and the box shows its spread. It answers how close two sequences must be to be called one clone.
    How to read: the threshold is fitted per subject from a bimodal distance distribution, so subjects differ. A subject far from the others fitted a weaker separation, so check its distance histogram in the report.
    Source: https://shazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/DistToNearest-Vignette/
  column: threshold
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: threshold per subject, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Threshold sensitivity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median sensitivity the chosen threshold achieves, and the box shows its spread across subjects. It answers how many truly related sequences the threshold keeps together.
    How to read: a low value means related sequences are split into separate clones. Shazam publishes no minimum, so compare subjects with each other.
    Source: https://shazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/DistToNearest-Vignette/
  column: sensitivity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: sensitivity per subject, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Threshold specificity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median specificity the chosen threshold achieves, with the lowest and highest across subjects. It answers how well unrelated sequences stay apart.
    How to read: when the run fixes the specificity as the selection rule, every subject sits at that value and the card only confirms it. Otherwise a low value means unrelated sequences risk being merged into one clone.
    Source: https://shazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/DistToNearest-Vignette/
  column: specificity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: lowest and highest specificity

- component: table
  title: Threshold table
  description: |-
    Each row is a subject with its fitted model, the chosen threshold, the sensitivity and specificity it reaches and the mean threshold applied across subjects. It answers which model and threshold each subject got.
    How to read: compare the subject threshold with the mean threshold, which is the single value the pipeline applies.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: v_gene_heatmap
  title: V gene usage by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is a sample and a V gene: the fraction of its sequences that use that gene. Rows and columns are clustered. It answers which samples share a V gene repertoire.
    How to read: samples that cluster together use V genes in similar proportions, as expected for the same subject or locus. A sample that clusters away from its subject may carry a skewed or contaminated repertoire. Dark columns are V genes used by most samples.
    Lines and annotations: the strips beside the rows name the subject and the locus of each sample.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: row_id
    row_annotation_cols:
    - subject_id
    - locus

- component: table
  title: V gene usage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and locus, with the fraction of its sequences using each V gene. It answers the exact usage behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a gene column to find the samples that use it most.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: v_usage_composition
  title: V gene usage composition
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment a V family or V gene, sized by the share of the sample's sequences that use it. It answers which V segments dominate each repertoire.
    How to read: switch between the family and the gene level with the rank control. Samples with the same segment proportions are similar. A segment that takes a large share in one sample only may point to a clonal expansion using it.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Fraction of sequences
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: seq_freq

- component: card
  title: V genes by family
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct V genes seen in view, and the bars rank the V families by how many genes they contribute. It answers how broad the V gene usage is.
    How to read: a family with many genes seen has a broad usage. A short list means the repertoire uses few segments, or the samples are shallow.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: v_family
  top_n_count: 5
  filter_expr: col('rank') == 'V gene'
  caption: V genes seen, by family

- component: table
  title: V gene usage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a V family or V gene in one sample, with its sequence count and its share of the sample's sequences for that locus. It answers the exact usage behind the bars.
    How to read: filter by rank to compare families or genes, and sort by share to list the dominant segments.
